D.t: Dan Ahlers trails by 14.8 and wins 4% of simulations. Closing it takes about 28,487 voters switching sides, or 56,973 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +23.9 and R +5.2. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The polls page average is R +18.0. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners (D) at R +12.7; your worst is Mason-Dixon for South Dakota News Watch and USD Chiesman Center at R +19.2. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Minnehaha, a projected net 4,032 votes; Oglala Lakota, a projected net 2,628 votes; Todd, a projected net 1,506 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Minnehaha, D +4.8, 21.7% of the vote; Brown, R +8.7, 4.0% of the vote; Brookings, R +5.2, 3.6% of the vote; Yankton, R +11.8, 2.6% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Dan Ahlers runs furthest behind in Hughes, Lawrence, Butte. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 91% of voters, 40 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.57 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 74% of voters, 41 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.71 points; Voters without a degree, 64% of voters, 41 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.19 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Dan Ahlers: Immigration voters 15 to 83, Incomes $125K and up 35 to 64, Voters who can afford daily costs 37 to 61. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
Registered Democrats cast 30% of the 73,571 ballots in South Dakota so far, against 53% for the other party. That is 5.3 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
